# Xenon Design System (Zx)

> Xenon is a dependency-free design system for browser applications; Zx is its product-agnostic
> vanilla-JavaScript implementation. ES2022 modules, WAI-ARIA-accessible controls built on native platform features,
> semantic `--zx-*` design tokens with light/dark theming and one token-driven geometry, and
> lifecycle-safe components. Source modules run directly in the browser; a build step emits ESM, IIFE-global,
> ZeyOS binding, and CSS bundles. Zero runtime dependencies.

Instantiate every component as `new Component(target, options)`, where `target` is an Element, a
selector string, or `null` (the component creates and owns its root, retrieved via
`.toElement()`). Subscribe with `.on(type, fn)` or an `on<type>` option; handlers receive a
`CustomEvent` whose `.detail` is an object. Call `.destroy()` to clean up. The same API is
available as ESM named exports and as `window.zx.*`.

## Documentation site
- [Documentation](docs.html): the documentation surface — getting started and every component.
  Each entry shows a live demo, its complete JavaScript source, and the API reference.
- [Getting started](docs.html#getting-started): installation, the mental model, theming,
  accessibility, and talking to ZeyOS.
- [Components](docs.html#components): components organized into task-based sections, with entries
  alphabetized inside each section.
- [Layouts](layouts.html): the layout gallery, each layout running live with its full source.
  Application templates — mail, an issue tracker, a knowledge base, an AI chat, an invoice editor,
  an item and inventory record, a workflow tool, an infrastructure dashboard, and a CRM — built on
  one shared application shell; and screen patterns — master–detail, dashboard, inbox, record page,
  two wizards (vertical and horizontal steps), settings workspace, and a schema-driven ZeyOS
  invoices screen. `layouts.html#<id>` opens one directly (`#crm`, `#zeyos-invoices`).

## Deeper references
- [Agent reference](../docs/llms.md): per-component constructor options, methods, and events for
  every component plus the core helpers. Sections are marked `<!-- doc:<name> -->`.
- [README](../README.md): what Zx is, quick start, component index, theming, browser support.
- [Changelog](../CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release, including behaviour changes an
  upgrade has to account for.

## Start here: choosing
- Start every screen from the closest **layout**, never from a blank page. Gallery:
  https://zx.zeyos.com/layouts (`layouts.html#<id>` opens one); source
  `https://zx.zeyos.com/layouts/<id>.layout.js` + `<id>.layout.css`; the shell helpers
  `layouts/kit.js` + `kit.css`, and `layouts/overview.js` + `overview.css` (`createOverview()`,
  the toolbar-chips-drawers-pager composition every record screen uses). They are site modules,
  not package exports: copy them beside the application.
- Templates (complete applications on one shell): `mail`, `issue-tracker`, `wiki`, `ai-chat`,
  `agent-workspace`, `invoice-editor`, `item-inventory`, `workflows`, `infrastructure`, `crm`.
  Patterns (single screens): `master-detail`, `record-collection` (any list of records),
  `dashboard`, `inbox`, `record-page`, `agent-chat`, `record-wizard`, `checkout-wizard`,
  `settings-workspace`, `system-states` (every empty, loading, error, and confirmation state),
  `zeyos-invoices`.
- The agent reference's **"Choosing what to build with"** section maps each screen to its layout
  and each job to its component, lists the theming decisions (theme, accent preset, geometry
  tokens, material, motion, colour roles), and what never to build by hand. Read it before
  building anything.

## Components
- Inputs: `button()`, `buttonGroup()`, `badge()`, `CheckButton`, `Toggle`, `Search`,
  `Select` (APG combobox;
  `filter: false|'local'|async`; priority, status, permission, and `Select.entity()` presets),
  `Checklist`, `TagPicker` (icon/color identity),
  `NumberField`, `Rating`, `Slider` (native range; marks, bounds, optional number box),
  `copyButton()`/`CopyInput`, `DatePicker`, `MonthPicker`, `TimePicker`, `Datebox`/`DateTimeBox`,
  `DateRangePicker`/`DateRangeBox`,
  `Timebox`.
- Overlays: `Tooltip`, `Message` (toasts/inline/progress), `Modal`, `Dialog` (+ `alert`/`confirm`/`prompt`
  Promises), `Sheet` (edge-anchored Dialog; `side`, `modal: true|'trap-focus'|false`, `backdrop`,
  `snap` detents, swipe-to-dismiss), `SheetStack` (drill-down; `stack`/`cascade`), `Dropdown`,
  `MenuButton`, `ContextMenu` (right-click and Shift+F10; `selector` gives per-row menus from one
  instance).
- Data: `EntityRef` (dense linked/static identity), `FileItem`/`FileList` (durable and transient
  file presentation), `ActivityItem`/`ActivityList` (chronological entries and grouped feeds),
  `Table` (sortable, selectable, sticky header, opt-in inline editing, row reorder, column
  visibility), shared `RecordView` state through `TableView`, `CardView`, and `KanbanView`, `Grid`
  with single-click editing and `Grid.BillingItems()`, engine-neutral `Chart`
  with injected `ChartJsAdapter`, `Calendar` (agenda/day/week/month/year, pointer/keyboard drag and
  resize, `optimistic: true|false`), backend-neutral nested `Filter`, simple client-side `DataFilter`,
  `FilterPanel` (typed filters from server field metadata), `ListToolbar` (search, count, view
  switch, badged tools), `ViewSettings` (field order, visibility, grouping, board axes),
  `Pagination`, `SortControl`, `TreeView` (APG tree),
  `Finder` (Miller columns).
- Forms: `Form`, `Fieldset`, `Questionnaire` (guided one-question-at-a-time flow with branching), `Field` (type registry), `CodeEditor` (structured text,
  never executed or injected), `ValueList`, `MultiValueEditor`, `FieldUpload`.
- Layout: `stack()`/`grid()`/`aspect()`, `Groupbox`, `Card`, `StatTile`/`statTile()`, `AppIcon` (generic tile geometry;
  circular `zeyosAppIcon()` application presets and compact `moduleChip()` identities),
  `Aurora` (one- to four-colour ambient
  canvas light; shared material roles govern chrome and overlays), `Avatar`, `Panel`, `MasterPanel`, `Tabbox`,
  `NavigationBar`, `AppSidebar` (expanded/minimized vertical and horizontal rail states; sections; a
  modules layout), `ModuleBar` (colour-coded module strip or bar with flyout menus and an "All
  modules" catalogue),
  `AccountMenu`, `WorkspaceSwitcher` (workspace tile, name and menu at the head of a navigation
  column), `Launcher`, `spinner()`/`ProgressBar`/`InlineLoading`,
  `skeleton()`/`skeletonText()`/`skeletonTable()`, `Toolbar`, `SplitView`, `Dock` (collapsible
  resizable pane stack; tab groups,
  regions, adopts a `Sheet`), `Stepper`, `Breadcrumb`, `emptyState()`.
- Core: `Component`, `h`/`__`/`icon`, `position`, `breakpoints`/`breakpointOf`/`matchBreakpoint`/
  `onBreakpoint`, i18n, date utilities, `defineElements` (declarative `<zx-*>` custom elements).
- Helpers: `formatNumber`/`formatCurrency`/`formatFileSize`/`formatRelativeTime`, `storage()`,
  `toCsv`/`downloadBlob`/`copyToClipboard`, `truncate()`/`isTruncated()`,
  `groupBy`/`sortBy`/`uniqueBy`, `throttle`,
  `debounce`, `uid`, `deepMerge`, `clamp`, `toArray`, `isElement`, `htmlEscape`,
  `formatDate`/`parseDate`/`addDays`/`addMonths`/`clampDate`/`isSameDay`/`getWeekStart`,
  `translate`/`printf`/`setTranslator`/`setLanguage`, `focusTrap`/`rovingTabindex`/`typeahead`.

## Theming
Load `zx.css` once and put `zx-scope` on the application root. Set `data-zx-theme`
(`light`|`dark`|`auto`) on any ancestor. There is one geometry: spacing steps are multiples of
`--zx-space-unit` (4px), radius steps are fractions of `--zx-radius` (4px), and controls are
`--zx-control-height` (30px) tall; override those to tighten or loosen an application. Define a
product theme by overriding semantic `--zx-color-*` / `--zx-control-*` tokens under
`[data-zx-theme="name"]`. Never use tier-1 palette tokens or raw colour literals in application
CSS. The stock themes use a restrained neutral ramp with the ZeyOS green as the accent.
Six stable accent IDs ship as `data-zx-preset` (zx, zeyos, ocean, violet, rose, slate). The theme
studio applies complete recipes spanning accent, neutral tint, spacing, font, type size, radius,
control height, and the CSS-first material — Glass (the default, a thin lit pane), Deep glass,
Frost (milk glass), Smoke (tinted), Paper, Satin and Enamel (opaque, no blur), or Flat, each a
token-override recipe composed from the theme's glass ingredients — with the result exportable
as CSS. Compact menus,
pickers, tooltips, column menus, and toasts use responsive compact glass; Launcher, Modal,
Dialog, and floating Sheets use a calmer reading panel. Both preserve scoped theme inheritance and
refract Aurora/page content; docked Sheets and dense data surfaces remain opaque.

## Talking to ZeyOS
Use the dedicated ZeyOS client library **`@zeyos/client`** (`npm install @zeyos/client`) for ZeyOS
business data: `createZeyosClient({ platform, auth })`, typed
`client.api.list/get/create/update<Resource>` over the full OpenAPI surface, `normalizeListResult`.
The optional `zx-zeyos` binding (`src/zeyos/`) generates typed tables, forms, and pickers from
`client.schema`; it never imports `@zeyos/client` itself and ships as a separate bundle.
The `ZeyOS invoices` layout is the reference integration. Zx also ships a minimal `Http`/`zeyosService`
for ad-hoc in-app `remotecall`, but `@zeyos/client` is the recommended default.

That optional entry also maps schemas into Table, Card, and Kanban record views. Its
`SavedViewRegistry` adds private named configurations scoped by user, workspace/fork (null means
the base workspace), and resource through an injected atomic transport. A compatibility adapter
reuses authenticated ZeyOS `userfields` without persisting records, selection, pages, callbacks,
or DOM.

## Installing
`npm install @zeyos/zx` · `import { Table } from '@zeyos/zx'` · `import '@zeyos/zx/zx.css'`.
Entry points: `.` (components), `./zeyos` (schema-driven ZeyOS binding), and `./global`
(classic script tags).

## Commands
`npm run serve` (no-build site at http://127.0.0.1:8321/website/docs.html) · `npm test` (unit
tests + token lint) · `npm run build` (dist bundles) · `npm run build:site` (deployable site).
